(Add more information to Sets sections on season pages) by Wikifan988[]

Inspired by something Toa said from the collectible items vote, I think it could be useful to have a paragraph in the Sets sections of each season (and pilots and DOTD) page, where it would talk about the significant traits of the sets and how closely they relate to the season. The mention of a mascot character would me moved here, and this is where collectible items would me mentioned. It would explain which aspects of the show the sets focus on, and if there are significant settings in the season that are not featured in the sets or significant differences between the sets and the season, such as how there are no Ivory City/Kingdom of Shintaro sets in the S13 wave and how the Geckles and Munce are portrayed as villains in the sets. This could also explain more about the box art and branding surrounding the seasons, such as the note I added to the S4 page trivia recently about how the Tournament of Elements sets look to take place in a jungle setting even though the jungle is only the main location of a few episodes. It could also be mentioned which waves marked the beginnings and ends of various trends such as spinners, Airjitzu Flyers, etc. While these types of notes could all be in trivia, I think it could be helpful to have a section dedicated to it, in order to group similar information together and to have the trivia sections be more concise for other show-related information. Also, it could be more helpful for newcomers who are not as familiar with the set/show relationship and may not understand aspects of the series and sets that others have come to expect.

Support

  1. Great idea. I definitely agree. Legoninjagofan600 (talk) 15:53, 3 January 2021 (UTC)
  2. 100% on board with this idea.   LuigiMaster41    Talk    16:42, 3 January 2021 (UTC)
  3. SoyP777 (talk) 21:02, 6 January 2021 (UTC)

Oppose

Neutral

Comments

The result of the vote was: Support

(Allow users to vote for featured articles) by LuigiMaster41[]

Hello, Ninjago Wiki users! LuigiMaster41 here, and I want to propose an idea, to allow users to vote for featured articles. I don't believe there is an option of do so, so I think having a wiki page allowing users to vote for featured articles would be a great idea. Obviously, there should be rules on how articles can be featured, and what users need before they can nominate or vote for articles.

A nominated article should have
  • No notice templates, (Stub, Gallery Organization, etc.)
  • Must have been part of the wiki for 1-2 weeks
  • All required headlines per the Manual of Style, and all must be filled with the required information
For users to vote, they must
  • Have been part for the community for a month, and must have 300 mainspace edits
  • Sockpuppets must not be used to vote (obviously)
  • You cannot have been blocked as a result of vandalism or spam

If there are anymore rules that could be added, please let me know, I would love to hear your feedback! Also, I think nominations should last for 3 days, and added maximum of 4 articles can be nominated at once, but only 1 will pass.

Again, please let me know your suggestions below!

Support

Oppose

  1. I honestly don't think we need to make a vote for feature articles due to nobody mentioning feature articles. Instead, a user can suggest an article. Also, if we were to vote, I don't think we need "special rules" to determine feature articles. Printer89 (talk) 03:01, 8 January 2021 (UTC)

Neutral

  1. SoyP777 (talk) 22:52, 8 January 2021 (UTC)

Comments

Hmm, I like your point, Printer. If this proposal doesn't pass, I can take your idea of having users suggesting articles into consideration. Though I would like to ask, why shouldn't we have "special rules" to determine featured articles?   LuigiMaster41    Talk    13:51, 8 January 2021 (UTC)

Because I think it's easier to ask instead of having a vote with another set of rules. Printer89 (talk) 22:20, 8 January 2021 (UTC)

Ah, I see what you mean. Thanks for explaining your view. I'll wait to see what other users think. If this proposal does not pass, then we can make it to where users can ask for an article to be featured.

  LuigiMaster41    Talk    22:32, 8 January 2021 (UTC)

The result of the vote was: Oppose


(Add design sections to character galleries) by Wikifan988[]

This idea is inspired by how Brickipedia has "Gallery of variants" sections for characters, including "Non-physical variants" sub-sections, and this is also done on some non-LEGO wikis such as the Ben 10 wiki. I think it could be good to have a section on this wiki in character galleries where all of the character's different TV series appearances are shown. This is because the Minifigures and TV series designs are two different things (for example, Dragon Master Jay is not in the show, and TV host Jay is not in the sets), and because a significant amount of Ninjago fan activity involves discussing and comparing the various character designs and appreciating the obscure costumes that characters have worn for various reasons. Having a gallery like this would allow readers to look at all the TV series designs in one place without having to scroll through an entire character gallery.

  • I imagine this would be the first sub-section under "In LEGO Ninjago: Masters of Spinjitzu," under a heading called "Designs" or "Design variants" (though I'm up for suggestions).
  • These sections should probably only exist in galleries for characters with more than five designs.
  • I realize the Appearance section on character pages covers the overall designs, but this would be a place for every different outfit and appearance the character has had over the course of the series, as if each of those designs was its own Minifigure.
  • Here are some of these galleries I've worked on so far, though not all of the designs are included here yet.

Support

  1. I definitely agree. In fact, I've thought about it for a long time. It is true that people often want to see different variants of non-physical minifigures, but browsing galleries is often too complicated. Legoninjagofan600 (talk) 8:12, 12 January 2021 (UTC)

Oppose

Neutral

Comments

The result of the vote was: Support


(Change "Influence" to "Legacy") by Wikifan988[]

On every other wiki I've seen, this type of section is called "Legacy", not "Influence". (I know other wikis are not the main reason to do something, but I think in this case it is one good reason because "Legacy" sounds better and it's good to be consistent with other wikis when possible.) I originally thought Influence would be a better name because it applies to characters both living and dead, but for most living characters, it is not necessary to have an additional section for one or two lines of information that could be in Trivia instead. From my perspective, "Influence" implies the character is still around and interacting with other characters regularly, which is not the case with most of the characters who have this section. Apart from Garmadon, Jay's mother, and Aspheera, all of the characters with one of these sections are deceased, and I think it would be fine to have the sections for these other three characters be called "Legacy" as well: Garmadon was deceased at one point and has mostly not been present in general society, Jay's mother is unaccounted for so her role in the story is more or less the same as if she was not alive, and Aspheera was inactive for a thousand years and has later had an effect on the ninja's memories as shown in several episodes. Also the Ninjago franchise uses the word "Legacy" to refer to things that are not over or gone, in the Legacy subtheme and in this video, so it makes sense to use the term for these cases on this wiki.

Support

Oppose

  1. If they are not deceased, it looks weird to call it Legacy.Ninja72 (talk) 15:16, 17 January 2021 (UTC)
  2. On par with Ninja here.   LuigiMaster41    Talk    15:19, 17 January 2021 (UTC)

Neutral

  1. Samurai viper (talk) 16:41, 17 January 2021 (UTC)
  2. SoyP777 (talk) 18:33, 17 January 2021 (UTC)

Comments

Then can we call it something else or include it in biography sections for those characters, and call the other ones Legacy? Wikifan988 (talk) 15:20, 17 January 2021 (UTC)


Yeah, I would be alright with that.Ninja72 (talk) 15:24, 17 January 2021 (UTC)

Ok cool, I think "Impact on other characters" would be a good option because it's clearer what the section is about. Wikifan988 (talk) 15:37, 17 January 2021 (UTC)

The result of the vote was: Oppose

(Overturn Separation of Weekend Whip vote, other stuff) by Printer89[]

First of all, I would like to introduce our newest friend, The Fold Wiki. This wiki aims to provide information about The Fold from their latest albums as well as The Weekly Whip.

With that being said, I think we should overturn this decision which would involve deleting all of remixes and putting the information on The Fold Wiki. Permission was granted to allow another vote. An example can be see here.

Also, there is information scattered throughout the wiki (e.g. mentioning Dan's mother) which relates more to The Fold rather to Ninjago. I feel like we should remove those type of information and include it on The Fold Wiki.

Support

  1. Samurai viper (talk) 16:41, 17 January 2021 (UTC)
  2. Ninja72 (talk) 18:33, 17 January 2021 (UTC)
  3. I did not agree with this decision to seperate the pages in the first place, and now with the new wiki in mind, my vote will not change. NinjaBrix (talk) 00:04, 18 January 2021 (UTC)

Oppose

  1. We should keep the remix pages, because it's better to have a page for every song that is individually released, especially since there are so many lyric variations and different trivia, and having them all on one page would make The Weekend Whip page too long. Also the trivia would be too much if it was merged. I get what you mean about how we could link them, as we do do that for other content such as Chima, but in that case it's because the content is not relevant to the Ninjago franchise itself, whereas in the case of The Weekend Whip remixes, we should keep all of them because they are equally relevant to Ninjago as they are to The Fold. This is similar to how there are pages for Ninjago characters on Brickipedia- even though they could link to the Ninjago Wiki instead, it's also relevant to Brickipedia, so there are pages there even if it means there is mostly duplicate information on both wikis. It is still directly relevant to Ninjago and there is enough variation between the remixes. Even though the lyrics aren't changed in all the remixes, they're almost always arranged in different ways, which means they each deserve their own pages and lyrics. However I do agree that information should not really be included about The Fold unless it is relevant to Ninjago. Wikifan988 (talk) 16:39, 17 January 2021 (UTC)
  2. Even if we have the new wiki, we must be listing all official info related to Ninjago, so my vote will not change here. If they are removed, such information here could become less reliable.   LuigiMaster41    Talk    18:26, 17 January 2021 (UTC)
  3. TitaniumNinja74 (talk) 02:28, 18 January 2021 (UTC)
  4. I think they should stay separate because they are different and this makes it clearer. There are also character pages from Ninjago on Brickipedia, although there could simply be a link to our wiki. As with Brickipedia, there is only a brief overview and more detailed information on The Fold Wiki. Legoninjagofan600 (talk) 15:38, 22 January 2021 (UTC)

Neutral

  1. SoyP777 (talk) 18:33, 17 January 2021 (UTC)
  2. Yeah, I'm not sure. While we should have all Ninjago content here, the changes in the songs tend to be fairly minor. --Toa Kopaka Nuva (talk) 10:46, 20 January 2021 (UTC)

Comments

I feel like most of the remixes are the same lyrics with very few differences. Also, the ninja's pages have very long trivia and have much more content that The Weekend Whip. And if the info is too long, then we can put it on The Fold Wiki. Printer89 (talk) 16:53, 17 January 2021 (UTC)

Good point, that is true about the trivia. However, the lyrics are usually ordered very differently, which is just as significant as if they were entirely different lyrics, in my opinion. For example, the Chris Lord-Alge mix lyrics, Rebooted Whip lyrics, and Anacondrai Whip lyrics are all ordered differently. Also I think the fact that they were released as separate songs makes a strong case for why they should be separated, because they exist as individual products/releases with different release dates and information. For example, The 2014 Michael AM Remix as a song is the same level of significance as After the Blackout, so it does not make sense to treat them differently because one is based on a pre-existing song. Wikifan988 (talk) 16:58, 17 January 2021 (UTC)

They are all essentially remixes and even if they are ordered differently, I don't think it's significant enough to have an additional page. Printer89 (talk) 18:37, 17 January 2021 (UTC)

The lyric variations need to still be listed somewhere though, other than Trivia because that does not cover all of it. Wikifan988 (talk) 22:38, 17 January 2021 (UTC)

If all the lyric variations aren't included somewhere on the wiki, information is being omitted because they are still technically different songs and with different arrangements of the lyrics. However, including all the lyrics on one page would be too much. Because neither option is preferable, I think the best decision is to keep the page separated. Wikifan988 (talk) 18:30, 18 January 2021 (UTC)

A comparison would be if a "snake characters in TV shows" wiki was created and every Serpentine character was given a page there, that would not be enough reason to remove the individual Serpentine pages from this wiki. Even though many of the Serpentine soldiers have nearly identical minor roles and they could technically be summarized on one page and we could link to the snake characters wiki instead, it would be inconvenient and would make this wiki less reliable and easily accessible. Also it feels strange to have pages for such minor things like Mister Whiskers but not individual pages for the different Weekend Whip remixes, which are very major as separate songs in the realm of Ninjago music. Wikifan988 (talk) 14:11, 20 January 2021 (UTC)

Since my reasons for why they should stay separate are scattered across the previous paragraphs, here is a summarized version of these reasons:

  • The remixes are different releases/products and have different release information (similar to the Legacy sets being different from the original sets) and all of the remixes are directly related to Ninjago and were released connected to the Ninjago brand
  • The lyrics vary widely (see these three for example), and they need to listed somewhere, but one page would be too long and Trivia cannot effectively cover it all
  • Another wiki having pages does not mean our wiki should remove pages if they are still relevant to this wiki (for example, a "snake characters in TV shows" wiki would not mean this wiki's pages for Serpentine should be deleted)
  • It is strange to have pages for such minor things like Mister Whiskers but not individual pages for the different Weekend Whip remixes, which as individual songs are very major in the realm of Ninjago music and individually appear across different episodes
  • The way it was before was fine, but having them separated has been neater and better-organized and has more information such as lyrics, release date, and more concise trivia
  • This is not one of my points from before, but the Ghost Warrior pages are not merged with each other even though many of them are simply different arrangements of the same things

Wikifan988 (talk) 22:39, 21 January 2021 (UTC)

(Rename video pages) by Wikifan988[]

I propose we change the name of Blooper Reel - LEGO Ninjago to "2011 blooper reel," Exclusive Blooper Reel! to "2014 blooper reel," LEGO NINJAGO Movie Outtakes and Bloopers to "LEGO Ninjago Movie blooper reel" or "The LEGO Ninjago Movie blooper reel," That's a wrap - Season 13 Outtakes & Bloopers - NINJAGO Dungeons of Shintaro to "Season 13 blooper reel," and LEGO NINJAGO Explained: Everything You NEED to Know about LEGO NINJAGO to "Ninjago honest trailer."

While this may seem counterintuitive at first, it would be better for organization, linking, and search engine optimization. The first two blooper reel names are very unspecific and could potentially refer to any of them. The S13 blooper reel and honest trailer names are very long and are almost always referred to by these shorter names anyway, so the coding is always something like [[That's a wrap - Season 13 Outtakes & Bloopers - NINJAGO Dungeons of Shintaro|Season 13 blooper reel]].

Furthermore, their current names are pretty random. The movie bloopers are titled differently on the LEGO YouTube channel and the Cartoon Network channel, indicating there is not really one concrete way they're supposed to be named and that the names were simply chosen on the spot or based on sounded the most "eye-catching" to whoever was tasked with uploading the video.

I can see a concern for this being that there it would be inconsistent with the rest of the wiki, but in fact there are already other pages whose names are something other than their official names. For example, Fugi-Dove's brother is called "Criminal #1" in the credits, but his page isn't named that because it would be confusing and more of a pain for readers to find and for editors to link to. I think it's the same with these videos, where even though their current titles are technically correct, they are less convenient for basically every other reason and thus should be given more concise and specific titles.

Oppose

Neutral

(Create the following categories) by Wikifan988[]

The following is a list of categories that I think would be beneficial to add to the wiki.

  • Exclusive minifigures/characters (characters who appear in only one set)
  • Boats (since there are categories for bikes, jets, etc)
  • Four arms (Stone Army Mech, Mech-enstein, all four-armed characters)
    • While other appearance-based categories such as "Brown hair" are unnecessary, four arms is a recurring physical trait that is acknowledged in the series multiple times and at this point is a well-known trope of Ninjago characters/villains, so many readers may be interested to have a way to easily look through all Ninjago characters and vehicles with four arms.
  • Groups
  • Islands (Dark, Chen's, Tiger Widow, Dyer, Uncharted)
    • Same general idea as the Temples category or other location-based categories such as Realms
  • Pets (Rodrigo, Anacondrai serpent, the original dragons, Chompy, etc.)
  • Non-speaking characters (Circus Clown, Elemental Master of Shadow, Cole's grandfather, unknown Elemental Master, Cyren, Mr. Righty Tighty, etc.)
  • Characters only appearing in sets (Jesper, snake villain, Moe, citizens from Ninjago City Gardens)
    • May need another title; possibly re-worded to include characters who appear in sets and other media but not the show, such as Claire
  • Legends of Chima (since there's a LEGO Dimensions category)
  • Statues (Cyrus Borg statue, titanium statue, Jadeblade statue, Cliff Gordon's replica)
    • This is because there are a number of times where have symbolic or story significance in the series. We could also possibly include the Stone Army pages
    • The category could also be expanded to include statue-based locations such as the Hall of Villainy and Heart of the Mountain
  • Delayed minifigures (or another title) (minifigures who appeared in show before the sets: Soto, Misako, Dareth, most of the Elemental Masters, etc.)
    • Similar to and equally as notable as Characters without a minifigure
  • Lists (List of characters, List of cast and characters, List of reused designs, etc.)
    • Useful form of navigation/organization
  • Twist villains (Brad Tudabone (Double Trouble), P.I.X.A.L. (The Surge), Pythor (Rebooted), Fenwick, Krux, Harumi, Zane, Vangelis)
    • Same type of category as Redeemed Characters
  • Living main antagonists (I've seen notes about this in page Trivia sections, but I think since there ten of these now it would be better to have as a category and remove the note from trivia because it is fairly common)

I realize not everyone may agree on all of these so let me know if there are ones in particular that you think should not be created so we can discuss it but still have create the others if this vote is supported.

Support

Yes. Slab, Chompy, etc. are never called by these names in the sets either, while they are never called Earth Dragon, Wu's Battle Dragon, etc. in the show. Generally it's a precedent on this wiki that names from the show are prioritized over names from te sets.

If pages aren't allowed to be named after nicknames or names that the characters/creatures did not have from the beginning,, we should rename Grundles to Dromaeosaurid Theropod Grundalicus, Chuck to Unnamed Yang student, Crabby to Unknown crustacean creature, Adam to Plundar's spider, and so on. This would be counterintuitive and unnecessary, because the names they have are the ones they're known as and the ones most people know them as because the show calls them this.

The orginal four dragon pages were named the way they are because in the past, Ninjago was a smaller theme with fewer characters and creatures, so there was only one of each dragon this names could be referring to. However, as the theme has expanded year after year, it becomes necessary to reasses this both for distinguishing them from other pages and for being consistent with how other pages are named. Exactly. If there were no other dragons from the First Realm with the same names, it wouldn't be so necessary. (Make parentheses lowercase) by Wikifan988[]

Since we now have many lowercase page titles, I think it would be the best decision to change page names with parentheses notes to having those notes be lowercase. For example, changing The Royal Blacksmiths (Episode) to The Royal Blacksmiths (episode). This is because they are not part of the proper names themselves and are simply there to discern between pages. This is something that's done differently across different wikis, but I believe the lowercase choice is the better option.

A while ago I was the one to capitalize some of these to make it consistent across pages, but I realize now that it would have been better to make them all lowercase. At the moment there are already some with lowercase parentheses notes: Nindroids (ninja faction), Nindroids (Digital Overlord faction), Arcturus (rocket), as well as all disambiguation pages. While these are currently the minority, it would be more consistent with everything else format-wise to have the pages changed to lowercase notes.

While it may feel strange to those who have been used to the uppercase ones for a while, it's important to remember when this is simply due to familiarity vs which is the best decision regardless of what's been done before. Toa said he would be fine with using his bot to change the links, or even just leaving them, since the titles aren't really shown on pages and most people probably would not notice the redirects. Either way this would make the wiki more logically-formatted and consistent in the long run.

  2. Legoninjagofan600 (talk) 09:50, 1 March 2021 (UTC)
  3. Keeping it smooth A man has fallen into the river in LEGO City! 23:13, 2 March 2021 (UTC) (ignore the signature I use)

(Rename LEGO Ninjago to Ninjago (TV series)) by Wikifan988[]

Looking at various sources including the show itself, it appears the show is not called LEGO Ninjago or LEGO Ninjago: Masters of Spinjitzu, but simply, Ninjago or Ninjago: Masters of Spinjitzu. For example, the word "LEGO" is nowhere to be seen anywhere in the title cards, and at least half of the distributors (Cartoon Network, Foxtel) don't list LEGO in the name. So, while it would be a massive change, I think it would be best to rename the page to Ninjago (TV series). A bot could be used to change the two most common uses - ''[[LEGO Ninjago]]'' and ''[[LEGO Ninjago|LEGO Ninjago: Masters of Spinjitzu]]'' - to ''[[Ninjago (TV series)|Ninjago]]'' and ''[[Ninjago (TV series)|Ninjago: Masters of Spinjitzu]]'' respectively, which would massively cut down on the number of links that would need to be changed manually. Along with this, it would be a good idea to change Ninjago (sets) to something like LEGO Ninjago (toyline) or simply LEGO Ninjago (though if this was the case it would have to be done after all the TV series links were changed, to avoid confusion). This is because the boxes and LEGO.com and toy-related media say "LEGO Ninjago" and have the LEGO logo.

Support

  1. I'm on board with these ideas and agreed with all the reasons stated above. And yeah, we can simply use a bot to change the links. Because of these reasons stated, I'm keeping my vote in support.   LuigiMaster41   Talk    20:59, 18 April 2021 (UTC)
  2. I agree with everything. Also, it never made sense to me why the show is called LEGO Ninjago and the theme is called Ninjago (sets), when it should be the other way around (with the word LEGO) Legoninjagofan600 (talk) 05:35, 19 April 2021 (UTC)

Oppose

Neutral

Comments

But this is just one idea, I'm open to others as well. Wikifan988 (talk) 23:15, 19 April 2021 (UTC)

I don't think we should give a disambiguation to both since that will cause more pipelinking and pipelinking is a very annoying thing.Ninja72 (talk) 23:30, 19 April 2021 (UTC)

It seems to have been supported based on the idea that the character/object/whatever appeared in a comic. However, from what I am seeing on the Ship Wrecked! page, it seems the Keepers did not appear in the comics of the magazine, Stranded, which takes place right after the Season 13 finale and features the Bounty crashing somewhere, the ninja fixing it and continuing their flight. So what I am suggesting is that magazine first appearances should only be counted if it was in the comic of the magazine, because otherwise they did not appear in an actual story. I think we should also remove the magazines from the appearances sections (unless the article subject has appeared in the comic of the magazine) to be more consistent with how the Character Encyclopedias and Visual Dictionaries are not listed in appearances sections.

(Include mentions in appearances) by Wikifan988[]

This may sound unnecessary but hear me out. I used to be glad that this wiki didn't include mentions as appearances as some other wikis do but after giving it some thought over several months I believe it would be helpful. This is partly because while uninterested fans could skim over the appearances that say (mentioned), it would be helpful and convenient for fans who are interested to see it.

This is because fans may want to know if characters were mentioned before or after their appearances. For example, Krux was mentioned in Seabound, which is not something you would otherwise know from his page, but is a bit of information about his character that's worth noting somewhere. Ray was mentioned by Kai and Nya several times before his debut, and this is part of his character's history as part of the show even if he didn't truly appear until much later.

Some things to note:

  • I realize mentions are not technically appearances of something, but it is probably similar enough to other things listed in appearances (pictured, voice, etc.) that it would be fine. Other wikis also often list mentions as appearances so it is generally understood even if not technically the right phrase - it would simply be unnecessary to have a whole other section for it.
  • This would apply to all location/vehicle/etc. pages, not just characters.
  • In the first appearance section in infoboxes, mentions would not count as appearances. Categories would also not be given to pages simply for mentions.
  • Mentions such as "our parents" or "my parents" (Kai in Day of the Departed, Jay in Game Over) could be listed as indirect mentions. However, phrases like "every villain we've ever faced" would not count as a mention for every villain. There are probably less clear instances like times when Jay may have said "my friends" in Skybound but those could probably be worked out on a case by case basis.

Support

  1. A well reasoned argument. PyrokineticNinjaMaster6913 (talk) 20:06, 21 June 2021 (UTC)
  2. As the idea proposed here wants to help out fans and readers with information, I'm on board with this idea.   LuigiMaster41   Talk 06:56, 22 June 2021 (UTC)

An area that is is lacking on the wiki is information regarding non-english dubs. Beyond different voice actors, these dubs have also occasionally changed the cuts of certain episodes. My thought is that each season could have their own subpage detailing information about dubs. (Ie: Seabound/dubs). These pages would then be divided into sections for the individual dubs. And it could also be used on Kai's page:

Etymology[]

The name, Kai, means "strong," "victorious," and "recovery," in three Asian cultures, all of which fit his hotshot attitude in the ninja's battles. His name may also be derived from the Japanese word Akai, meaning "red." In Scottish, Kai's name means "fire"; matching his elemental power. In Japanese, Kai's name also means "ocean," which annotates his mother's and sister's water abilities. In Hawaiian, Kai's name also means "sea", a further link to his mother's and sister's water abilities. Names Kai originally had were Dante and Ash, with Ash being the name The Hageman Brothers originally suggested. The name was not used because it was already the name of the protagonist of the Pokémon franchise. Ash was later said on LEGO.com to have been a nickname for Kai when he was young, As Tommy Andreasen was the one who wrote this description in 2012, it can be considered canon.

And Vinny's:

Etymology[]

The meaning of the name Vinny is "prevailing".

And Wu's:

Etymology[]

The meaning of a Chinese name Wu is 'military, martial' or 'affairs, business'. Legoninjagofan600 (talk) 06:52, 12 July 2021 (UTC)

This is definitely useful. PyrokineticNinjaMaster6913 (talk) 09:26, 12 July 2021 (UTC)

(Deal with the "powerful beings" fact) by Samurai viper[]

By looking at the edits regarding the strongest characters in Ninjago, like Lloyd as the Golden Ninja or Garmadon with his True Potential, I think it needs to have a major discussion, due to the fact that we missed a few and/or leads to speculation in some cases and later gets removed. For example, we first said that Wojira was a powerful character, but it later got removed because of this.

We also see some characters who were implied to be powerful but didn't include them, like Zane, Hazza D'ur, and Vangelis. And if I remember correctly, all three were able to take over an entire region for year's:

  • Zane defeated two armies within seconds by using a Forbidden Scroll, and later took over the Never-Realm for around 60 years.
  • Vangelis forced the Munce and Geckles to mine Vengestone from the Dungeons of Shintaro by using a skull that had Hazza D'ur's Dark Magic (which was said to have great power), and was later sold to keep the Kingdom of Shintaro.
    • And by looking at one of Bragi's tweet, Vangelis was considered to be one of Ninjago's baddest villains when it comes to strength, but not strong as the "worst villain".

Support

  1. Personally I believe these facts should be removed altogether, as power-scaling is on the speculative side. In my opinion the best we can/should do is list each character's powers and let readers decide for themselves who should be considered the most powerful, and there are other wikis such as VS Battles Wiki if one is interested in power-scaling for characters. There are some situations where Tommy has given his opinion (Nadakhan vs. Cryptor, Lloyd vs. Cryptor, Nadakhan vs. Overlord), but as we know, even the creators can disagree with each other and change their opinions over time. Also, the facts on these pages may consider characters to be considered because they have defeated other powerful beings, but power may not always be the only factor that determined who won. For example, one could argue that if Lloyd was not as emotionally invested in his fight with True Potential Garmadon, he would have been able to defeat or at least stalemate him. However, I am open to alternate ideas for all of this as well. Wikifan988 (talk) 05:08, 21 August 2021 (UTC)

Lime

(Add a "Connections and effects" sub-section in the ability pages) by Samurai viper[]

After reading The Book of Elemental Powers, I actually noticed that we barely talk about the fact that somethings are known for being influenced by the power (or the other way around). I mean, we did something like that to the "connections between elements" section in the Elemental Powers page, but we never thought about including how of the powers (elemental or not) effects things in their respective pages and vice versa.

And by that, I'm saying we should create a sub-section in each of the abilities' pages that shows how they affect (or is connected to) other things (people, places, etc.).

  • Examples (note: this is not how it will actually be placed):
    • In Way of the Departed, it was revealed that Edo magic (a form of Dark Magic) is connected to Airjitzu, which is the reason why the ninja don't use Airjitzu. Or in the Realm of Madness, Garmadon went there to find a way to possess all four Golden Weapons at once, and Dark Magic gave him four arms to do that.
    • Some places such as the Desert of Doom or the Never-Realm, Water Elementals have a difficulty of using their power due to the fact that the regions are known for affecting water. However, Water Elementals have the ability to control the marine life or merge with the Endless Sea, because both of those things are related to water.
    • In The Island and Seabound, it was revealed that the power of Storm is known for effecting the Endless Sea in a bad way and the reason why the Island of the Keepers was uncharted in the first place. Because the storms within the storm belt caused several ships and planes to disappear every they went there.
      • In addition, the full power of Wave and Storm was described to be the chaos and destruction that engulfed Ninjago's realm before the First Spinjitzu Master arrived.
    • After discovering an Elemental Power, Vex erased Zane's memories and tricked him into using his power of Ice on the people of the Never-Realm.
    • Because of having the element of Time, the Time Twins became villains after believing they had a strongest element and attempt to rule Ninjago. And after the Battle for All of Time, Time became an element that anyone can use by possessing an artifact.

(Properly deal with naming vehicles) by JayTVStudiosYT[]

This has been a common debate within the Ninjago Wiki's discord server, which is what we should name vehicles. The current rule and what most vehicles follow is to name what they are called in the show (Lightning Bike, Ghost Cycle). However, when I asked to rename the Storm Fighter to the "Storm Glider," Toa Kopaka Nuva noted that most people know it as the set name and it's possible the "Storm Glider" is a mistake.

I suggest we should create a policy about this to deal with it once and for all. I will put three options to vote on: set names, show names (unless they don't properly describe the vehicle), or don't make a policy.

In my opinion, we should go with the show names option. There is a great deal of the fanbase that doesn't buy the sets but does watch the television series and knows the vehicles from the show names alone. They are also said quickly and can be passed along by word of mouth rather than the set names which are just written. However, we should name the vehicle the set name if the show name is inaccurate, for example, the Lightning Jet being called the "Lightning Mech." Magic Blast, Crystal Ball, Star Fall! (Vote for deleting pages) by Legoninjagofan600[]

I don't think the way deleting pages using the Candidate for deletion template currently works perfectly. It often happens that someone puts this template on the page and nothing happens for a very long time. No one expresses whether they agree or disagrees with the deletion, and if so, it takes a very long time for the page or template to be removed from the page. Therefore, I think it would be appropriate to vote on every page that someone thinks should be deleted. It would be voted in a completely classic way, and the one proposed by the deletion must explain why he wants to delete the page. In this way, the deletion would take place relatively quickly and would always be decided by a vote and not just a discussion. What do you think?

After rewatching Master of the Mountain, I began to think that we should actually changed Shintaro back to Shintaro Mountain. Examples:

  • Example 1

Postman: Heh, you got an invitation. To Shintaro!

Lloyd: Shintaro?

Postman: Mm-hmm, the Ivory City!

  • Example 2

Lloyd: Shintaro? As in, Shintaro?

P.I.X.A.L.: As in the remote and exclusive mountain kingdom of Northern Ninjago.

Zane: Invitations to Shintaro are exceedingly rare. In recorded history, there have only been a handful of outsiders allowed into the Ivory City.

Jay: I've heard it's incredible! It's the most beautiful city in the world.

  • Example 3

Vangelis: Welcome, welcome! I'm most pleased you were able to accept our invitation. It is an honor.

Wu: The honor is ours. Shintaro is beyond anything we imagined.

Also in Vangelis' description in the Character Encyclopedia New Edition, referred Shintaro as the kingdom instead of the mountain. And in the synopsis of "Into the Dark", it said that "Princess Vania reveals a secret entrance that leads to an underground mine beneath Shintaro" not within.

In addition, the characters never used the term "Shintaro" for the mountain, they just call it... the mountain (I don't why, they just do).

  • Example 1

Vania: Thank the mountain.

  • Example 2

Vangelis: I'm very disappointed, Vania. It is forbidden to enter the mountain.

  • Example 3

Gulch: Ah, it began with the three explorers. Three adventurers who ventured deep into the mountain, into the old tunnels where all Geckles are forbidden to go.

  • Example 4

Vania: Hailmar, listen. My father is lying to you. He's using you! Cole and these men, they were betrayed by my father. They were cast into the mountain.

  • Example 5

Vangelis: Your friend did come to me. And I cast him into the bowels of the mountain.

(Reform account policy) by Printer89[]

I think we should change our account policy. Currently, you are allowed to have more than one account, but cannot have another account to evade a ban, cause disruption, and gain an advantage in voting. However, here are some of the disvantages of our current policy:

  • Hard to keep track of who's who
  • Can cause inaccurate results when trying to poll/discuss issues
  • Can cause people to create more accounts since it's hard to juggle multiple accounts and they may forget they have alt accounts; leads back to first problem
  • Can cause people to get into more trouble if they get blocked and accidentally use an alt not knowing the blocking policy
  • Inconvenient if we're having to block multiple accounts just because of one account

And because of this rule, it has caused confusion on having multiple accounts. One example was with Mysteryman3177 (now known as Frost Formling). Before the clean start policy was added, this user thought he could "move" accounts and take on a completely different personality without having to tell anyone. This became a problem because the Mysteryman account was prohibited from making a request for rights and by having a different account, he was able to make multiple requests for rights and nearly became the bureaucrat for this wiki. And since you can have more than one account, he probably thought what he did was perfectly fine. His Mysterman account was also never blocked when he "moved" nor did he cause a community disruption, so you can understand where he's coming from.

To combat the previous issue, I added a clean start policy but it contradicts our current policy of having multiple accounts. Users can easily abuse this rule by doing what Frost Formling did or claim that their alt accounts are not there's and still use it since you're allowed multiple accounts.

So with that being said, I believe users should only have one account at a time. Bigger wikis like the Creepypasta Wiki have implemented a similar policy, so it's nothing new. I understand users may want to contribute with multiple accounts just in case their main account glitches or has issues, but that's when you need to contact Fandom for help. My experience with Fandom has been good as they have been able to respond to my issues within 24 hours. Also, this rule hasn't been paid attention to us admins. Even when I "added" the rule this year, me, Toa Kopaka Nuva, and Quinton1721 have still blocked users for having more than one account - even though users weren't evading a block or causing community disruption. It would be a lot easier for the admins and for you if we had this rule to create a safe and healthy community.

Support

  1. Samurai viper (talk) 20:17, 22 December 2021 (UTC)
  2. Yes, this is a smart move and I am 100% supporting this. I do have one question though; what would be the rule if a user has forgotten their password?   LuigiMaster41   Talk 20:28, 22 December 2021 (UTC)
  3. I definitely support this but have the same question. Person from Ninjago \ 22:38, 22 December 2021 (UTC)
  4. Legoninjagofan600 (talk) 07:38, 23 December 2021 (UTC)

Oppose

  1. Frost Formling once told me "sometimes sockputtery rules have to be a little flexible" in one of our conversations after he revealed that he was Mysteryman, so I am pretty sure he knew that what he was doing was not allowed, he just did not care.Ninja72 (talk) 10:04, 23 December 2021 (UTC)

Neutral

  1. SoyP777 (talk) 17:39, 24 December 2021 (UTC)

(Add Credits section to crew member pages) by Wikifan988[]

I propose that on crew member pages, we add a section called Credits that is essentially an Appearances section for crew members. There are already sections like this on some pages, such as here, here, here, and here, but they are not all consistent and it would be useful to have an organized strategy for these pages. For actors, all their episode appearances would be listed and it would say which characters they played, which would be helpful because otherwise if you wanted to see every episode certain actors appeared in and which characters they played, you would have to go to the Appearance sections of the pages of each individual character voiced by those actors. The Credits sections would also note when voice appearances were archival, uncredited, etc.

Here is an example for how an actor's Credits section would look, and here is one for how an author's would look. You may notice that in these examples, there are subsections for the types of roles the crew members have (for most there are only one role, but sometimes there are crew members who are both writers and producers for example, so this allows for the crew member's different roles to be listed separately). I believe we should take this approach as well—even though most crew members only have one role such as actor, writer, and so on—because it would make it clear once again what role the crew member had and would allow for multiple credits sections for crew members like Tommy Andreasen who have been both a writer and producer, for example.
